name: Kbd
description: A key or shortcut shown as the user would press it, marked up as <kbd>. Use one element per key; put separators between keys in a combination so the order stays clear when read aloud.
researchNote: Documents a shortcut; it does not register one. Nested <kbd> marks each key in a combination.

elements.name: Key label
elements.description: The key name or glyph, such as Esc, Enter or ⌘

elements.name: Combination
elements.description: Several keys with a text separator such as "+"

variants.caption: Sequence — then another key
variants.htmlOutline: Press G then I to go to the inbox.

usageNotes: Use <kbd> only to show keys or shortcuts people should press. Don't use it for product names or generic badges.
For a combination, nest a <kbd> per key (or use adjacent keys with a text "+") so screen readers hear each key, not one run-on word.
Always say what the shortcut does in nearby text. The styled key alone is not enough for people who can't see the visual treatment.
Kbd documents a shortcut; the page still needs a real keyboard handler if the shortcut should work.
Prefer plain key names (Ctrl, Shift) when the audience may not know platform glyphs, or match the user's platform when you can detect it.
frameworkNotes: Verified Nov 2026 against each live index. Chakra UI, Radix Themes and shadcn/ui ship Kbd. Polaris React had Keyboard key; current Polaris web components point apps at native kbd instead. Apple HIG Keyboards covers physical keyboards and system shortcuts, not a key-label control.
